text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Kenya Polytechnic is closed indefinitely after at least 3,000 students boycott classes and engage police in violent confrontations.
- The opposition proposes among other things, the immediate establishment of a broad-based national consultative council to discuss the timetable for effecting constitutional reforms.
- Controversial Islamic preacher Sheikh Khalid Balala is given a hero's welcome upon arriving in his home town of Mombasa at the Kenyan coast.
- President Moi criticises a section of the opposition for pursuing "outdated politics" and cautions those issuing threats to the government.
- The treasurer of opposition National Development Party Omondi Oludhe declares he will support President Moi in the forthcoming general election.
- The battle for a presidential candidate from the Democratic Party of Kenya is set for July 31, begins with a call to Chairman Mwai Kibaki to step down.
- Sheikh Balala is evicted out of city hall for making a scathing attack against the government in the presence of city councillors.
- President Moi says public university vice-chancellors should facilitate dialogue for him with aggrieved students, whenever the need arises.

- Chairman of the ruling party Kenya African National Union (KANU) Ndolo Ayah says KANU will only meet elected opposition leaders in their capacities as party officials for dialogue over constitutional reforms, and not party activists.
